label: Hyperactive Agency Detection
notes: Tendency to attribute intentional agency to ambiguous events or non-agentic entities, foundational to many explanations of belief in gods/spirits (Boyer, Atran)

label: Mnemonic Transmission Enhancement
notes: Narrative features (e.g., repetition, rhyme, vivid imagery, minimally counterintuitive elements) that improve memorability and fidelity of cultural transmission

label: Group Identity Reinforcement
notes: Narratives that foster in-group cohesion, define group boundaries, or create a shared collective identity (Henrich, Atran)

label: Moral Regulation & Norm Enforcement
notes: Myths encoding, justifying, or illustrating social norms, ethical guidelines, and consequences for transgressions, often policed by supernatural agents

label: Cooperation Facilitation
notes: Stories, beliefs, or associated rituals that promote pro-social behavior, trust, and collective action within a group (Henrich, Norenzayan)

label: Threat & Anxiety Management
notes: Narratives or ritual prescriptions that address existential threats (death, disease, disaster), reduce psychological uncertainty, or provide frameworks for coping

label: Minimally Counterintuitive (MCI) Concepts
notes: Presence of a small number of violations of intuitive ontological expectations (e.g., talking animal, thinking object), making narratives attention-grabbing and memorable (Boyer)

label: Ritual Binding & Costly Signaling
notes: Myths that structure or give meaning to ritual acts, especially those involving costly displays that signal commitment to group norms and beliefs, enhancing trust (Atran, Henrich, Sosis)

label: Intuitive Ontology Manipulation
notes: Myths that leverage or slightly violate intuitive knowledge about folkpsychology, folkbiology, or folkphysics to create compelling narratives (e.g. purity/pollution leveraging folkbiology)

label: Status Hierarchy Legitimization
notes: Myths that explain, justify, or naturalize social stratification, leadership roles, or power differentials within a society

label: Social Learning Bias Exploitation
notes: Narratives that capitalize on evolved social learning biases (e.g., prestige bias, conformist bias) for their transmission and acceptance (Henrich)

label: Supernatural Prosocial Punishment
notes: Belief in supernatural agents who monitor and punish selfish or anti-social behavior, thereby supporting cooperation and norm adherence
